newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler offers $1,000 incentive on minivans.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler offers $1,000 incentive on minivans.

text.p: Chrysler Corp., acknowledging stiffer competition in a weaker U.S. minivan market, said Wednesday it is raising cash incentives on its minivans to up to $1,000 from $595 previously.

Chrysler said the new programme, which runs through July 7, offers $1,000 cash allowances on long-wheelbase versions of its 1996 and 1997 Dodge Caravan, Plymouth Voyager and Chrysler Town & Country models and $750 on short-wheelbase versions.

The Chrysler move follows recent decisions by Ford Motor Co. and General Motors Corp. to offer new retail incentives on their compact sport utility vehicles, and adds to Wall Street analysts' concerns that profit margins in the lucrative light truck segment will erode.

Detroit's Big Three can attribute most of their booming profits over the past four years to pickup trucks, sport utility vehicles and minivans. They have lost money on some traditional passenger car lines.

Salomon Brothers analyst John Kirnan said in a research report Wednesday that he expected Chrysler to "join the parade" of sport utility incentives on its Jeep Cherokee and Grand Cherokee models within the next few days.
Chrysler spokesman Michael McKesson said the company has no plans to add cash incentives to the Jeep models.

While sport utility vehicles once sold at robust rates without any incentives, automakers began offering subsidised lease payments on them over a year ago. Analysts expect the cash incentives to grow as competition, particularly from Japanese automakers, increases.
GM is offering a $1,000 rebate on its Chevrolet Blazer and GMC Jimmy models, while Ford is offering subsidised, 4.8 percent financing on its Ford Explorer and Mercury Mountaineer vehicles.

Chrysler said the new minivan incentives replaced a programme that expired Tuesday that offered a free sliding driver-side rear doors to minivan buyers, a $595 value. Although the new programme offers a higher cash value, the fourth door is once again an extra-cost option.

Chrysler's minivan sales for the first four months of 1997 were down 4 percent from a year earlier to 168,982 vans. The vans face new competition from a trio of new minivans from GM just as overall sales in the minivan segment are declining.
U.S. minivan sales this year through April have fallen 3.1 percent to 395,154 units, according to J.D. Power and Associates.

"I'd have to say that it has peaked, but it's still a huge, important market," said George Pipas, Ford's sales analysis manager. Ford is offering a $1,000 rebate plus 7.9 percent financing on its Windstar minivan.

Chrysler still dominates the minivan market segment, and James Holden, the company's executive vice president of sales, service and marketing, said the incentives are aimed at holding on to Chrysler's nearly 43 percent share of the market.
"This sale will allow consumers to buy the best for even less and keep Chrysler, Plymouth and Dodge minivans at the top of the segment," Holden said in a statement."
